title: Calculus II and an introduction to multivariable calculus
stage: College neuroscience and cognitive science degree
audience: a college student in a neuroscience, cognitive science, psychology or biology degree program, or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Extend calculus: techniques of integration, numerical integration, improper integrals, applications of integrals, sequences and series, power and Taylor series with error bounds, parametric and polar curves, and functions of several variables with partial derivatives, gradients and gradient descent.

weeks.1: Integration by substitution and by parts
weeks.5: Applications: area, volume and arc length
weeks.12: Partial derivatives, gradients and gradient descent

blocks.deliverable: Compare the trapezoid rule and Simpson's rule in code.
Compute volumes and limits of sequences.
Week 7 midterm; test ten series for convergence.
Approximate functions with Taylor polynomials in code.
Compute gradients and run gradient descent on a function.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Numerical methods notebook: implement in Python the trapezoid rule, Simpson's rule, Taylor approximations and gradient descent, test each against exact answers, and explain the errors you observe.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.

files.L01.txt: Integration by substitution and by parts
files.L05.txt: Applications: area, volume and arc length
files.L12.txt: Partial derivatives, gradients and gradient descent
